deliveroo.source: Deliveroo_Master_Consolidation.xlsx — Weekly Summary. + ops from Weekly Summary sheet

issues: Covers rose to 3,707, up 420 (12.77%) week on week.
Spend per head fell to £18.93, down £1.22 (6.05%), because of £5 ramen and free ramen redemptions (around 616 last week).
Sales were £81,256.30, up £5,771.28 (7.64%) week on week and £13,756.31 (20.38%) ahead of the £67,500 target.
Labour was 18.88% against a 21% target, with the budget rota projecting 20.82%.
Operational food cost was 24.30% against a 25% target; the site said £5 ramen pushed food cost up, and variance was all good.
Amy Tang praised the Manchester team for high £5 ramen volumes, in the region of 600 to 800.
Deliveroo improved last week but needs to be more consistent, and reviews are an area for improvement.
A delivery customer received only the cold bag and was missing dynamite prawns; the site has emailed them and offered a refund. A 3 star review has also been replied to.
At the BOH meeting, food Google reviews included 3 star ratings with no comments, and takeaway reviews were poor because of missing items.
Sophie raised earlier reviews about a spicy dish (transcribed as 'kagi'), dry and non-fresh sushi on 27/09 and a beef tataki complaint.
Sushi ratings were average, with one unclear rainbow roll complaint that Andrew Sud thinks may be nori absorbing cucumber moisture.
Avinash Peter warned that the upcoming promotions will spike food cost and labour.
Sophie warned that Meadowhall and Leeds borrowing stock from Manchester creates out of stock risk for Manchester.
A new glass washer has been installed and the old unit is due to be removed at the end of the week.
The front door repair is still pending.
The sound system is broken and there is no music: the engineer found the safe is overheating the amplifier and one amplifier cable is broken.
Inka Cheung asked for the sound system to be fixed as soon as possible regardless of cost, with a new safe if it cannot be fixed and a door left open for airflow rather than installing a cooler.
Air conditioning servicing is booked for 8:30 on 07/10.
The new deep fryer is too small and is waiting for Ross to exchange it.
A replacement fire extinguisher is still awaited.
Manchester was the only site to have sent Mapal compliance photos so far.
Intangibles and FOH and BOH staffing were reported as all good, with no recruitment needed.
Region-wide (England): the £5 ramen offer is now limited to one per person through a backend change, announced by Amy Tang at the 06/10 KPI meeting.

Region-wide (England): the Mapal compliance app (transcribed as 'Maple') must be installed on site laptops and iPads, with photos sent to the management chat; front of house staff may no longer use personal phones for compliance on shift, while kitchen staff may use their own phones.

Region-wide (England): table toppers must carry exactly one drink menu, one XOXO drink and one ramen loyalty card, and marketing material requests go to the England group chat for Amy Tang to forward to marketing.

Region-wide (England): at the 06/10 BOH meeting Sophie asked sites to top up stock through the promotions rather than hold back for food cost limits, to monitor dashboard stock levels, and to stop borrowing stock between branches.
